en: Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Magadha, in the Dharmāraṇya at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍala*), upon a lion throne with a lotus interior inlaid with vajra-jewels, together with a great host of bodhisattvas—bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten hundred thousand koṭī-niyuta buddha-fields beyond description.
Furthermore, at that time, in that very assembly of the bodhisattvas, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Acintyaprabharāja was present and seated among them.
Then, through the power of the Buddha, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Acintyaprabharāja rose from his lotus seat and addressed the entire host of bodhisattvas:

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon (*kalpa*) here in this Sahā world-system is but a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitābha, in the world-system Sukhāvatī.

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Kaṣāyadhvaja is but a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Suniścitapadmaphullitagātra, in the world-system Avaivartikacakranirghoṣā.

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Avaivartikacakranirghoṣā is but a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmadhvaja, in the world-system Virajā.

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Virajā is but a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Siṃha, in the world-system Pradīpā.

Indeed, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Avaivartikacakranirghoṣā is but a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmadhvaja, in the world-system Virajā.

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Virajā is but a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Siṃha, in the world-system Pradīpā.

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Pradīpā is but a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, in the world-system Suprabhā.

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Suprabhā is but a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmaraśmiprajvalitagātra, in the world-system Duratikramā.

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Duratikramā is but a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvābhijñāmatirāja, in the world-system Vyūhā.

Furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, what constitutes an eon in the world-system Vyūhā is but a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Candrabuddhi, in the world-system Ādarśamaṇḍalacakranirghoṣā.

"O sons of the Conqueror, by means of this entry into the calculation of world-systems, having passed beyond ten hundred thousand times the atoms of Buddha-fields, there is one day and night in the Buddha-field of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One Bhadraśrī, in the world-system Padmaśrī, wherein there is the specific cultivation of the stages for Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, whose conduct is universally auspicious."

"O sons of the Conqueror, whoever shall take up, preserve, recite, cultivate, master, and extensively proclaim to others this Dharma discourse that reveals the qualities of the Buddha-fields of the Tathāgatas, at the time of his death, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, will stand before him throughout the ocean-like expanse of the infinite Buddha-fields of the ten directions.
And he shall remember his past lives until he awakens to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Thus spoke the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acintyaprabharāja, who, being permitted by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, was filled with joy. And that entire assembly of Bodhisattvas rejoiced in what was spoken by the Bodhisattva Acintyaprabharāja.
Thus ends the seventeenth Mahāyāna sūtra, titled "The Manifestation of the Qualities of Infinite Buddha-fields," from the *Buddhāvataṃsaka*, the Vaipulya Piṭaka.
